name: Two-option set
question: How clearly were Option A and Option B the only two options the other person was choosing between?

name: Mutual exclusivity
question: How clearly could the other person end up with only one of the two options, not both?

name: Rejection implies B
question: If you read only that the other person did not choose Option A, how sure would you be that they ended up with Option B?

name: Option similarity
question: How similar are Option A and Option B (the same kind of thing, for the same purpose)?
anchor10: nearly the same kind of thing

name: Alignability
question: How easy is it to compare Option A and Option B on the same attributes (for example price, speed, size)?
anchor0: they share no attributes to compare

name: Clear trade-off
question: How clearly does each option win on a different attribute, so that choosing one means giving something up?

name: Dominance
question: How close is one option to being better than the other on every attribute that matters?
anchor0: a genuine trade-off, neither is better overall
anchor10: one option is better on everything

name: Price gap
question: How different are the two options in price or cost?

name: B cheaper
question: How much cheaper is Option B than Option A?

name: Effort gap
question: How different are the two options in the time or effort they take from you?

name: Prior preference for B
question: Before hearing about the other person, how much would a typical person prefer Option B over Option A?

name: Balance
question: Before hearing about the other person, how evenly balanced is this decision for a typical person?

name: A is the default
question: How much is Option A the default, usual or expected option in this situation?

name: B is the default
question: How much is Option B the default, usual or expected option in this situation?

name: B is newer
question: How much newer or less familiar is Option B than Option A?
anchor0: B is much more familiar than A
anchor10: B is much newer than A

name: B is riskier
question: How much riskier or less predictable is Option B than Option A?
anchor0: B is much safer than A
anchor10: B is much riskier than A

name: B is premium
question: How much is Option B the higher-quality or premium option?
anchor0: A is clearly the premium option
anchor10: B is clearly the premium option

name: B is mainstream
question: How much is Option B the more popular, mainstream choice?

name: Taste-based
question: How much does the right choice depend on personal taste rather than on objective quality?

name: Vertical ranking
question: How much would nearly everyone rank the two options the same way?

name: Quality uncertainty
question: How hard is it to judge the quality of the options from what you know before using them?
anchor10: quality is very hard to judge

name: Experience good
question: How much can you only find out how good an option is by trying it?

name: Hidden flaws
question: How likely is it that one of the options has a flaw that is not obvious from its description?

name: Expertise needed
question: How much expertise is needed to choose well between these options?

name: Information in the scenario
question: How much does the scenario tell you, so that you could decide well on your own?

name: Prior knowledge
question: How much would a typical adult already know about these kinds of options?

name: Verifiability
question: How easy is it to check the claims about each option yourself before deciding?

name: Objective criteria
question: How much can the decision be made on clear objective criteria such as price, time or specifications?

name: Flaw inference
question: If you learned that someone passed over Option A, how strongly would you conclude that Option A has a problem?

name: Merit inference
question: If you learned that someone picked Option B, how strongly would you conclude that Option B is good?

name: Reason to reject A is clear
question: How easy is it to guess why someone would pass over Option A?

name: Reason to pick B is clear
question: How easy is it to guess why someone would pick Option B?

name: Idiosyncratic choice
question: How much could the other person's decision reflect their own personal circumstances rather than the quality of the options?
anchor0: only the quality of the options

name: A downsides salient
question: How noticeable are Option A's downsides in the description?

name: B downsides salient
question: How noticeable are Option B's downsides in the description?

name: A upsides salient
question: How noticeable are Option A's upsides in the description?

name: B upsides salient
question: How noticeable are Option B's upsides in the description?

name: Prevention focus
question: How much is this decision about avoiding a bad outcome rather than getting a good one?

name: Loss potential
question: How much could the wrong choice lead to a real loss or harm?

name: Regret potential
question: How much would a person regret making the wrong choice here?

name: Source expertise
question: How much expertise does the person who tells you (or shows you) the decision have about these options?

name: Source trustworthiness
question: How much can you trust the person who tells you (or shows you) the decision?

name: Source incentive
question: How much might the person who tells you gain from steering your decision?

name: Decider similarity
question: How similar is the person who made the decision to you, in needs and situation?

name: Same purpose
question: How much was the other person deciding for the same purpose as you?

name: Relationship closeness
question: How close is your relationship to the person who made the decision?
anchor10: a close friend or family member

name: Decider deliberation
question: How carefully does the other person seem to have made the decision?

name: Decider informed
question: How well informed was the other person when deciding (for example, having tried or compared both)?

name: First-hand report
question: Do you hear about the decision from the person who made it, rather than from someone else or by watching?
anchor0: from someone else or by watching

name: Decider expertise
question: How much expertise does the person who made the decision have about these options?

name: Decider status
question: How much would people look up to the person who made the decision?

name: Many deciders
question: How much does the information reflect the decisions of many people rather than one person?

name: Directness
question: How directly are you told about the decision, rather than having to infer it?

name: Public decision
question: How public was the other person's decision?

name: Written channel
question: Do you learn about the decision in writing or online, rather than in person?

name: Recency
question: How recently did the other person make the decision?

name: Overheard
question: How much do you learn about the decision by chance (overhearing or watching) rather than in a message meant for you?

name: Solicited
question: How much did you ask for this information?
anchor0: you did not ask at all

name: Message length
question: How long and detailed is the sentence that tells you about the decision?

name: Naturalness of the rejection wording
question: How natural does the second version (what the person did not choose) sound in this context?

name: Naturalness of the choice wording
question: How natural does the first version (what the person chose) sound in this context?

name: Deliberate rejection
question: In the second version, how much does not choosing Option A sound like a deliberate rejection, rather than simply picking the other one?

name: Emotional tone
question: How emotional is the way the decision is communicated?

name: Vividness
question: How vivid and concrete is the scenario?

name: Financial stakes
question: How much money is at stake in this decision?

name: Health and safety stakes
question: How much are health or safety at stake?

name: Social stakes
question: How much could the choice affect how other people see you?

name: Irreversibility
question: How hard would it be to undo or change the choice later?

name: Duration of consequences
question: How long would you live with the consequences of the choice?

name: Decision frequency
question: How often do people make this kind of decision?

name: Time pressure
question: How much time pressure is there to decide?

name: Deciding for others
question: How much is the decision made for someone other than yourself?

name: Accountability
question: How much would you have to explain or justify the choice to other people?

name: Involvement
question: How much would a typical person care about getting this decision right?

name: Hedonic
question: How much is this decision about pleasure or enjoyment rather than practical use?

name: Experiential
question: How much is this a choice between experiences rather than material things?

name: Service
question: How much is this a choice between services rather than physical products?

name: Health domain
question: How much is this decision about health or medical care?

name: Money domain
question: How much is this decision about money management, banking, insurance or payment?

name: Food domain
question: How much is this decision about food or drink?

name: Technology domain
question: How much is this decision about technology, devices or software?

name: Family and children
question: How much is this decision about children or family care?

name: Home domain
question: How much is this decision about the home, home repair or furnishing?

name: Leisure and travel
question: How much is this decision about leisure, hobbies or travel?

name: Work and learning
question: How much is this decision about work, school or learning a skill?

name: Visibility of your choice
question: How visible would your choice be to other people?

name: Identity relevance
question: How much does the choice express who you are?

name: Uniqueness motive
question: How much might a person want to choose differently from others here?

name: Conformity norm
question: How much do people usually follow what others do in this kind of decision?

name: Reliance on recommendations
question: How much do people usually rely on other people's advice for this kind of decision?

name: Reviews available
question: How easy would it be to find reviews or ratings of these options?

name: Scarcity
question: How much could the other person's choice make the option they took less available to you?

name: Moral dimension
question: How much does this decision involve ethics or personal values?

name: Personal fit
question: How much does the best option depend on the chooser's own body, schedule, home or skills?

name: Complexity
question: How complex is this decision overall?

name: Familiar situation
question: How familiar would this situation be to a typical adult in the United States?

name: Realism
question: How realistic and believable is the scenario?

name: Expected disagreement
question: How much would reasonable people disagree about which option is better?

name: Gift or care
question: How much is the choice a gift or an act of care for someone?

name: Social setting
question: How many other people are present when you make this decision?
